hypotheses.title: Melatonin Extends Lifespan Through Circadian Photoreceptor Signaling
hypotheses.claim: Administration of melatonin extends lifespan in Drosophila melanogaster by activating the light-dependent circadian photoreceptor pathway. The lifespan extension depends on intact photoreceptor signaling.
hypotheses.rationale: Melatonin couples environmental light cues to circadian timing, and strengthened circadian signaling can improve metabolic and stress homeostasis. Enhanced photoreceptor pathway activity may thereby slow aging processes.
hypotheses.prediction: Melatonin-treated flies will live longer than controls, and the extension will be abolished when the light-dependent circadian photoreceptor pathway is disrupted.
hypotheses.experiment: Measure lifespan of melatonin-supplemented and control flies under normal light cycles and in flies with the circadian photoreceptor pathway genetically inactivated. A significant increase only in pathway-intact flies would confirm the claim.

hypotheses.title: Hydroxyprogesterone Caproate Extends Lifespan in Drosophila
hypotheses.claim: Administration of hydroxyprogesterone caproate extends lifespan in Drosophila melanogaster. Treated flies will show increased longevity relative to untreated controls.
hypotheses.rationale: Hydroxyprogesterone caproate modulates steroid hormone signaling, which influences reproduction, stress resistance, and metabolism. Reproductive and endocrine modulation is a recognized route to extended longevity.
hypotheses.prediction: Flies receiving hydroxyprogesterone caproate will exhibit a statistically significant increase in median and maximum lifespan compared with vehicle-treated controls.
hypotheses.experiment: Supplement the diet of age-matched Drosophila melanogaster cohorts with hydroxyprogesterone caproate and compare survival curves against vehicle controls. A rightward shift in the survival curves would support the claim.

hypotheses.title: Melatonin Shortens Lifespan in Drosophila melanogaster
hypotheses.claim: Administration of melatonin shortens lifespan in Drosophila melanogaster. Treated flies will show decreased longevity relative to untreated controls.
hypotheses.rationale: Melatonin strongly modulates circadian phase and light-dependent signaling, and misaligned circadian input can disrupt sleep, metabolism, and stress responses. Such disruption can accelerate physiological decline.
hypotheses.prediction: Flies receiving melatonin will exhibit a statistically significant decrease in median and maximum lifespan compared with vehicle-treated controls.
hypotheses.experiment: Supplement the diet of age-matched Drosophila melanogaster cohorts with melatonin and compare survival curves against vehicle controls. A leftward shift in the survival curves would support the claim.
